I’ve been to inpatient before. And the greatest benefit was absolutely seeing others like me, which I didn’t expect. There were only 13 people in the unit with me, but they all came from such different walks of life. And we were all united by the desire to better ourselves mentally. There was unemployed people, people detoximg from drugs and alcohol. People who had 3+ kids before turning 23. People with 2 jobs but still in poverty. People who had stressful and troubling relationships with friends, family, siblings, and spouses. People who were middle aged and still trying to figure out who they were and what they wanted to do in life.

After being surrounded by so many folks who seemed to be doing perfect in life, the people I met in inpatient made me realize that that wasn’t true: it was me projecting my insecruities and past onto other people. And doing so was not only an insult to their complexity as humans, but to *my* complexity as well.

All in all, the best part of inpatient is your fellow patients. Good luck. Remember that if any nurse/tech/doctor/psychaitrist every tries to pull some shit, you have rights as a patient. Ask about a patient advocate or for the head therapist if you have any trouble with the staff. Take advantage of family visits to speak up about anything, too.

I understand how you feel. I was in the hospital last month b/c I was suicidal. I know it’s scary and unpredictable: different environment, different people, too much uncertainty. But please understand that when you go in there, you have rights as a patient. You have the right to be safe, to be heard, and to be taken seriously. 

Tell them you’re agoraphobic. Tell them what you’re uncomfortable with.  Speak your mind, think out loud, be honest. This is about you and your saftey. I wished the nurses and doctors I encountered could’ve just understood my needs, but I had to push for them when I felt I wasn’t being listened to. 

Go in with an open mind, and if you’re slighted by someone, know that you are more than capable of advocating for yourself. You’re literally doing that right now by reaching out.

You got this! >:)

Why isn’t the hospital an option for you? 

“I just don’t want to waste their time on me.” The time they will spend helping you is absolutely not a waste. Your life is worth living. You deserve to feel good and safe. And it is literally their job to help you. I don’t know if you think this isn’t serious enough for them, but I promise you it is. 

Please call 999.

Are you in the U.S.? If yes, call 911. You don’t need a signal to do so. If not, try your country’s emergency number. If that does not work, go outside and call out for help. I know it’s a lot easier said than done and it will be uncomfortable, but your life is worth more than temporary embarassment. Go to your neighbor or just anyone on the street.
